images.title: Back where you started
images.purpose: Shows the hook trick on one number: add 3, double, take away 6, halve, and the start comes back.
images.composition: One horizontal row of five circles joined by four arrows, centred across the frame.
images.exact_structure: Five equal circles in one row, evenly spaced, joined left to right by four straight arrows. Circle 1 and circle 5 are filled reddish purple #CC79A7 with white numerals and both hold 4 (the label 4 appears twice, first and last). Circles 2, 3 and 4 have white fill and dark outline and hold 7, 14 and 8. Above the four arrows, in order: + 3, × 2, − 6, ÷ 2, in teal #0072B2. Nothing else is drawn. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, which is large and centred; no scenery, no people, no other text.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Whatever number you start with, this trick hands it back.

images.context: Hook picture for the chapter opener; the video poses the question, the picture shows one run.
images.teaching_notes: Ask: is it luck with 4? Leave the why for later concepts.

image_decisions.why: A single run of the trick, start and end in the same colour, makes the surprise visible at a glance.
